FAQ
Do we need a dedicated purple team to get started?
No. Purple teaming is a collaborative process, not a job title. AttackIQ supports virtual purple teaming using your existing red and blue team roles.
Can we safely run these exercises in production?
Yes. All tests use safe, non-disruptive techniques designed for live environments.
What if we don’t have a red team?
You can still run purple team exercises using prebuilt adversary emulations. Blue teams can lead, supported by threat intel or external partners.
Does this support compliance and reporting?
Yes. Results are mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and align with NIST, DORA, and Zero Trust frameworks for audit-ready evidence.

The CISO’s Guide to Purple Teaming
Although the name implies the elimination of blue and red teams as distinct entities, purple teaming does not typically involve integrating those groups on the organizational chart. Instead, red and blue teams continue to operate independently. A shift to purple teaming means that the still-distinct red and blue teams develop highly communicative, supportive, and cooperative relationships across the functional boundary.
